newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house OKs temporary labor bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house OKs temporary labor bill.

text.p: Brazil's lower house approved a bill creating a labor contract which eases the terms under which employers can hire temporary workers -- a measure the government hopes will reduce unemployment and bring more workers onto legally-registered payrolls, an official said.
The Chamber of Deputies voted 213-191, with four abstentions, in favor of the bill which establishes the measure formally known as the Temporary Labor Contract.
The bill now goes to the Senate.

The labor contract would reduce the cost of hiring by between 20 and 25 percent by lowering employer contributions for temporary staff hired for a maximum of two years, the bill's author, Dep. Jose Mendonca Filho, said.
Brazilian labor law currently does not distinguish between short- and long-term hires.
The bill includes safeguards to stop employers from firing existing staff and replacing them with new, short-term workers.
It also sets proportional limits on the number of employees that companies may hire under the new contract.
Employers in Brazil bear heavy non-wage labor costs, due mostly to a wide range of contributions they must pay for each employee.
About 30 million Brazilians work in the "informal sector," an unofficially registered area of the economy in which workers lack contracts and as such do not pay payroll taxes.
The government floated the idea of the temporary contract earlier this year but the bill was considered too sensitive for approval before October and November municipal elections.
